nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter, then uses it in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.

A message filter that assigns messages to different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of a user action.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into various folders for a user and stores first classification data in a persistent store.

A model generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, maintained exclusively in non-persistent memory on a user's client device and not stored on disk or in another persistent data store.

A device that executes the passes of the multi-pass message filter, holds second classification data in non-persistent memory, and provides an interface enabling a user to select and execute the multi-pass message filter.<SEP>A user's computing device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and where the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute.

A device configured to receive messages, assign them to different message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network to the message folders.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver and processor operative to manage delivery of messages over a network and perform the multi-pass filtering actions.

A plurality of different folders to which messages are assigned and sorted, and to which a user may move an identified incorrectly sorted message.<SEP>A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and inspected during the passes.

Email messages that are sorted into folders and analyzed, including sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, contents, and attachments.<SEP>A plurality of communications received over a network, assigned to message folders, and scored by the multi-pass message filter.
A list or identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, presented to the user so misclassified messages can be moved to a different folder.
A memory-resident-only storage location where the generated classification model resides exclusively and from which it is purged.
A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.
A medium including data and instructions that, when executed on a computing device, provide for managing messages.
A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform the message filtering actions.

A book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, whose message sender's address may be analyzed to generate second classification data.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that may be analyzed to determine whether a message sender's address is present.

A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and to select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface on the client device.<SEP>A person for whom messages are sorted into folders and who is presented misclassification information to move messages.

A message filter executed in multiple passes on sorted messages; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message and identify messages sorted into incorrect message folders.

Data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train it; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device and is deleted upon providing the display of information.
Data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter when assigning messages to message folders.
A memory store at the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.
A communications network over which messages are communicated to the message folders.
A header of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
The content of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
A state of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
